title: SKEWED SCORE: A STATISTICAL FRAMEWORK TO ASSESS AUTOGRADERS

bias_targets.methodology: Using Bayesian generalized linear models (GLMs) with an interaction term between the grader identity and the evaluated LLM (index-based coding) to detect if an autograder systematically assigns higher scores to text generated by its own underlying model.

Incorporating the token-length difference between two model outputs as a continuous predictor variable in a binomial GLM to quantify whether an autograder systematically prefers longer responses during pairwise comparisons, regardless of actual quality.

bias_targets.target: Machine-generation bias (Human vs. Autograder scoring differences)
bias_targets.methodology: Applying a hierarchical GLM with grader-level effects nested in grader type (human vs. autograder) to identify systematic baseline differences (e.g., leniency or strictness) between human experts and LLM judges.
